data.title: S&P 500 materials sector: Four companies miss EPS estimates, six fall short on revenue
data.description:
Twelve of the 24 S&P 500 Materials-sector companies have reported third-quarter 2026 results this week. On the earnings front, four companies fell short of analyst expectations, while six missed revenue estimates.

Here’s a look at how the companies performed:

Among the major reporters, Freeport-McMoRan , which carries a 5.6% weighting in the index, topped Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue.

Freeport-McMoRan reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.88, beating consensus by $0.05. Revenue increased 8.3% year-over-year to $7.55 billion, exceeding estimates by $150 million. The performance was supported by higher realized prices of $6.54 per pound for copper and $4,273 per ounce for gold.

LyondellBasell reported mixed results, with both earnings and revenue falling short of expectations. Adjusted EPS of $2.54 missed consensus by $0.01, while revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $8.50 billion but came in $390 million below estimates. The chemical producer faced weaker demand and lower polymer prices but generated $1.7 billion in operating cash flow and completed a planned €500 million debt repayment.

Nucor delivered its strongest quarterly performance in more than three years, supported by robust domestic demand and higher realized steel prices. The steelmaker reported Q3 revenue of $11.25 billion, up 32% year-over-year and $460 million above consensus. However, adjusted EPS of $5.80 missed analyst expectations by $0.03. Steel mill shipments exceeded 7.2 million tons, while free cash flow reached $1.6 billion. Management expects fourth-quarter earnings to remain stable or increase modestly from Q3 levels. Nucor shares gained approximately 5% following the results.

Linde reported record third-quarter results, with sales rising 9.3% year-over-year to $9.4 billion and adjusted diluted EPS increasing 9% to $4.59. Both figures exceeded Wall Street expectations, with earnings beating by $0.07 and revenue by $240 million. Growth was supported by a 5% increase in underlying sales, including a 15% rise in the electronics end market. Backed by an $11 billion project backlog, Linde raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to 8%-9%.

Sherwin-Williams delivered mixed Q3 results, with consolidated net sales rising 7.9% year-over-year to $6.86 billion, ahead of analyst estimates. Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.63, however, missed consensus of $3.69, reflecting pressure from higher raw material costs, supply chain expenses and acquisition-related dilution. The company narrowed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $11.85-$12.15 and expects uneven demand conditions to persist into 2027.

Materials Earnings Calendar: Eight Companies Reporting Next Week

Eight S&P 500 Materials-sector companies are scheduled to report earnings next week, spanning three industries.

The Chemicals industry accounts for the largest share, with five companies on the calendar: Albemarle , Mosaic , Air Products and Chemicals , CF Industries Holdings and International Flavors & Fragrances . The Containers & Packaging industry has two scheduled reporters: Amcor and Ball Corp. . Meanwhile, Martin Marietta Materials is the sole company from the Construction Materials industry scheduled to report next week.

data.title: Ophthalmic products recalled: Why drug regulators ordered Sun Pharma to halt eye-drop production at Assam plant?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Indian drug regulators have directed Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, the country's largest pharmaceutical company, to stop manufacturing, selling and distributing ophthalmic products produced at its Assam facility after identifying significant deficiencies in its quality management system.

According to documents reviewed by Reuters, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) and the office of the Drugs Controller, Assam, issued the order on August 20 following a joint inspection by central and state drug regulators.

The action came after Sun Pharma voluntarily recalled around 11 eye-care brands, along with all ophthalmic products manufactured at the facility, in July. The regulators have also sought additional information concerning 332 batches of recalled ophthalmic suspension products.

In an internal notice sent to stockists at the time, Sun Pharma said it was withdrawing the products as a "precautionary measure."

The regulatory action followed a show-cause notice issued to Sun Pharma on August 10, highlighting shortcomings in its quality management system.

After examining the company's response, the authorities were not satisfied with the explanations provided and subsequently ordered the suspension of manufacturing, sale and distribution of all ophthalmic products from the facility.

The directive also means that Sun Pharma cannot restart ophthalmic drug production at the Assam plant until regulators examine and accept its compliance report.

The company has submitted a report outlining the corrective measures undertaken to address the identified deficiencies. An official familiar with the matter told Reuters that the regulator is currently reviewing the submission.

The regulators have sought further details regarding the recall of 332 batches of ophthalmic suspension products. These are liquid formulations commonly prescribed for treating various eye conditions.

"We voluntarily initiated a temporary cessation of manufacturing activities and informed the regulators," Sun Pharma said in a statement on Friday, adding that remedial measures had been put in place.

The recalled brands include Lotepred 1% 5ml eye drops, Nepalact OD eye drops, Nepalact-Z, Brinzotim eye drops 5ml and Depopred 2ml.

According to doctors, these medicines are used to manage eye inflammation, infections and chronic ophthalmological conditions.

Product packaging indicates that most of the affected medicines were manufactured at Sun Pharma's facility in Kokjhar village in Assam.

Industry experts estimate that the affected batches could involve hundreds of thousands of bottles of eye drops, reported Reuters.

Several questions surrounding the recall remain unanswered. It is not yet clear whether all the recalled products were contaminated, whether any of the affected batches were exported or whether patients reported adverse effects after using the medicines.

The regulatory documents reviewed by Reuters do not establish that contamination occurred across all recalled batches.

The developments come at a time when Sun Pharma is facing pressure on its financial performance. The company's ophthalmology business accounts for approximately 3% of its domestic revenue, according to its annual report for 2025-26. The segment is also among its important business areas in the US market.

Sun Pharma reported a decline in its second-quarter profit on Friday, partly due to a one-time charge associated with its acquisition of US-based Organon.

data.title: Intel wins multiple upgrades on SA after earnings-led selloff
data.description:
Intel fell more than 28% on Friday after its Q3 2026 results, as the semiconductor giant issued an underwhelming outlook for the current quarter, prompting multiple analysts to upgrade the stock on Seeking Alpha.

The selloff, Intel’s biggest since the 1970s, is a key buying opportunity, argued SA analyst Mike Zaccardi based on a technical analysis. “INTC remains higher by 87% for 2026, and the current plunge appears as a key technical buying opportunity in my eyes,” wrote Zaccardi as he upgraded the stock to Buy from Sell.

Analyst Bohdan Kucheriavyi upgraded Intel , noting that the company’s earnings report “was quite decent” given its topline growth of ~21% and the earnings beat of $0.12 per share on an adjusted basis. “The issue, though, is that Q4 is expected to be a much weaker quarter in comparison to Q3," the analyst wrote as they upgraded the stock to Hold from Sell.

Analyst Kenio Fontes’ upgrade was based on the stock's improved margin of safety following the selloff. “Now I’m comfortable enough to upgrade Intel to a Hold. Yet, I’m not seeing enough margin of safety to be bullish about the stock,” Fontes added as he upgraded INTC to Hold from Sell.

The Asian Investor also issued a similar upgrade, arguing that Intel’s valuation “has normalized” after the selloff, as the stock currently trades 50% lower than its year-ago level. “With Intel’s shares down ~50% from their 1-year high at ~$142, the valuation has returned closer to the chipmaker's historical average,” the analyst wrote.

However, Seeking Alpha Investing Group Leader Quad 7 Capital downgraded INTC to Sell from Hold, noting that the stock continues to trade at a level where “perfection is fully priced in, yet the forward picture is starting to show that high expectations are not being met.” “With full-year CapEx remaining heavy and Q4 earnings power decelerating rapidly, the stock's elevated premium looks increasingly unsustainable,” Quad 7 Capital argued.

data.title: CCI clears five major deals across food, energy, fintech and telecom sectors
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved five major proposed transactions across the food services, renewable energy, power infrastructure, financial services and telecommunications sectors, including deals involving Aditya Birla Renewables, Adani Energy Solutions, Prosus and Vodafone Group.

According to separate official releases issued on Saturday, the approvals cover mergers and acquisitions involving major Indian and international companies.

In the food services sector, the CCI approved the merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited with Devyani International Limited, bringing two major operators of KFC and Pizza Hut outlets in India under a proposed combined entity.

"The Proposed Combination envisages merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited (Sapphire) with and into Devyani International Limited (Devyani) and certain related transactions," the regulator said.

The merger, announced earlier this year, is expected to create a restaurant business operating more than 3,000 stores globally, with an annualised turnover of approximately Rs 8,000 crore.

In renewable energy, the CCI cleared Aditya Birla Renewables Limited's proposed acquisition of 100 per cent of Solenergi Power Private Limited from Shell Overseas Investment BV.

"The proposed combination relates to acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of the Target by the Acquirer from Shell Overseas Investment B.V. (Seller)," the regulator said.

The transaction, valued at approximately Rs 17,200 crore when announced in July, includes Shell's Sprng Energy renewable energy business in India.

The regulator also approved Adani Energy Solutions Limited's proposed Rs 3,050 crore acquisition of IntelliSmart Infrastructure Private Limited from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL).

"The Proposed Combination envisages the acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of the Target by the Acquirer," the CCI said.

The acquisition is expected to strengthen Adani Energy Solutions' presence in India's smart electricity metering sector.

In financial services, the CCI approved the acquisition of certain shareholding in Navi Limited by MIH Payments Holdings B V, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Prosus N.V.

Navi, founded by Sachin Bansal, offers financial services through a consumer-facing mobile application.

Separately, the regulator cleared the acquisition of a 16.2 per cent stake in Vodafone Group PLC by French company Vega SAS.

Vodafone Group operates telecommunications businesses across Europe and Africa and has a presence in India through Vodafone Idea Limited.

The approvals mark regulatory milestones for the proposed transactions, which remain subject to applicable closing conditions and other requirements before completion.

data.title: Bitcoin Fatigue Is Real: James Lavish Says Early Holders Have Moved On As Young Investors Turn To Betting
data.description:
Key points:
  • James Lavish said "there's a truth to the Bitcoin fatigue," as many early holders have sold and are "just not active anymore."
  • He said younger investors have moved money into prediction markets and sports betting.
  • Still, he said "the bottom is in," with a base case of Bitcoin topping out around $400,000 to $500,000 in 2029.

James Lavish said "there's a truth to the Bitcoin (BTC) fatigue," as many early holders of the cryptocurrency have sold and stepped away while its price struggled to break out. Lavish said younger investors once rotated between Bitcoin and altcoins, but many have now moved their money into prediction markets and sports betting instead.

Lavish, who co-manages the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund and serves as an independent director at Strive Inc. (ASST), said on Friday on the What Bitcoin Did podcast that he thought that it has gotten to “that point now where you've got so many of the original people who are in it sold enough that they're just not active anymore.”

"Everybody's on their phone betting 24/7," Lavish said, citing conversations with college students. He said many young people feel they "can't see how you're gonna get ahead," which pushed them toward riskier bets.

His comments came as Bitcoin’s price climbed up by 0.8% during the past 24 hours, trading around $77,300. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

Stuck Near $80,000

Lavish questioned why Bitcoin hasn't rallied despite rising U.S. debt, inflation of nearly 4% and higher oil prices, pointing to heavy flows into AI stocks and attractive yields on cash. Long-time holders selling call options also weighed on prices, he said, because market makers sold Bitcoin to hedge those trades.

Despite the fatigue, Lavish said he believed that the “bottom [was] in, and that we are back in that expansion cycle for Bitcoin." His base case was that Bitcoin would top out at around $400,000 to $500,000 in early to mid-2029. That was comparatively lower than his earlier call of $1 million by 2030 or 2031, he said.

Lavish has also been watching government debt markets closely. In August, as Bitcoin pushed past $67,000 after the U.S. Treasury doubled its long-dated bond buybacks, he had said that the U.S. Treasury had “blinked."

He expected interest in Bitcoin to return once prices recovered. "Once we get back over 100, you're gonna like the interest is gonna tick back up again," Lavish had said at the time.

data.title: Binance Details $6.3B Hot-Wallet Breach as Exchange Pledges to Cover Losses
data.description:
TL;DR: The company reported approximately $3 billion of affected assets frozen on-chain through coordination with issuers, investigators and other industry participants. Frozen tokens are not the same as recovered cash, and assets immobilized on-chain still require legal and technical steps to return.

Binance said unauthorized withdrawals began after its global hot-wallet infrastructure was compromised on October 29 at approximately 20:05 UTC. In its October 30 update, the exchange put the value of affected tokens at about $6.3 billion and said withdrawals were temporarily suspended pending additional security checks.

The announcement and the numbers

The most concrete starting point is the dated disclosure from Binance. It offers a specific basis for assessing Binance’s $6.3 billion hot-wallet breach without turning the story into unsupported price speculation.

The company reported approximately $3 billion of affected assets frozen on-chain through coordination with issuers, investigators and other industry participants. It said more than $6.34 billion of company resources were earmarked to absorb losses, with roughly $5 billion already held in the relevant tokens while it sourced the balance.

The development arrives as digital-asset markets remain sensitive to funding conditions, infrastructure reliability and the gap between promotional claims and operational results. It warrants attention on its own facts, without assuming a particular cryptocurrency must rise or fall in response.

Why the development matters

The question for market participants is what Binance’s $6.3 billion hot-wallet breach establishes today and what remains uncertain. An immediate reaction is not the same as evidence of a durable economic outcome.

For traders and institutions, the issue is not confined to the headline loss. A platform can promise balance-sheet compensation while users remain exposed to withdrawal interruptions, unsettled orders and uncertainty about the integrity of infrastructure on which they rely.

Users face two different forms of risk during a security incident. Asset losses are the direct financial concern, while withdrawals, service interruptions and unclear communications can make it difficult to assess or manage exposure. Investigations are strongest when confirmed technical evidence is separated from hypotheses about attackers.

Investors also need to separate changes in infrastructure from changes in token demand. Revenue may accrue to a company, a protocol treasury or a service provider without necessarily creating a one-for-one benefit for holders of a related token. Market impact depends on adoption, competition and the design of whatever fees or incentives are involved.

Risks the headline does not resolve

None of this removes the need for independent assessment. The published evidence identifies a development, while its risk and long-term economics are still open to examination.

Binance initially cited a potentially compromised laptop, but said subsequent work identified further points of intrusion. It stated that investigators had not found evidence that wallet private keys were leaked. That distinction leaves the precise authorization and infrastructure failure unresolved until a verified technical post-mortem is published.

Frozen tokens are not the same as recovered cash, and assets immobilized on-chain still require legal and technical steps to return. The exchange’s reimbursement commitment is an announcement rather than independently audited proof that every affected account has already been restored.

Security controls have to account for both malicious transactions and legitimate users who need access. Freezing, recovery and reimbursement mechanisms are not interchangeable: a frozen asset may be immobilized, a reimbursed user may be made whole, and a forensic investigation may still be incomplete.

The milestones to watch

The immediate checklist is relatively straightforward: look for verifiable implementation details and avoid interpreting a stated target as an outcome that has already occurred.

Binance said it was targeting a phased restart of withdrawals after security validation, planned an updated proof-of-reserves report by November 2 and expected to disclose further verified technical findings. Those milestones, rather than speculative attacker attribution, are the tests for the recovery process.

A durable signal would be consistent follow-through: actual usage, transparent reporting and a credible explanation of risk. Short-term token-price moves can be driven by macroeconomic conditions or leverage and may say little about whether the product or initiative succeeds over months and years.

From a market perspective, the first task is to separate the scale of the announcement from the scale of economic activity that has actually occurred. A company may report a large addressable market, an institutional name or a future capability, but those are not equivalent to settled transactions or recurring fee income. This is why the primary disclosure is a better starting point than a trading narrative attached to it.

Primary source: Binance’s primary announcement. This reporting reflects information available on October 31, 2026; targets, estimates and statements about future plans are attributed to their issuers.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Pharma company Gufic buys Lodha Avalon duplex in Juhu for Rs.236 crore
data.description:
BENGALURU, Oct. 31 -- A Rs.236-crore apartment purchase by pharmaceutical company Gufic Pvt. Ltd adds to a growing cluster of high-value residential deals at Lodha Developers' luxury project in Mumbai's Juhu neighbourhood, where pharmaceutical promoters and business executives have emerged as prominent buyers.

Gufic has bought a duplex apartment in the under-construction Lodha Avalon project for Rs.236.33 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey. The 14th-floor apartment has a carpet area of 19,694 sq. ft and comes with 10 parking spaces. The transaction was registered on 21 October.

The deal values the apartment at approximately Rs.1.2 lakh per sq. ft, making it one of the notable high-value residential transactions in Mumbai's luxury housing market.

Gufic, represented in the transaction by its director Vipula Jayesh Choksi, purchased the property from V Hotels Ltd, an entity acquired by Macrotech Developers Ltd, now known as Lodha Developers, through a resolution approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

Lodha Avalon is being developed on the site of the erstwhile Centaur Hotel, subsequently renamed Tulip Star.

The transaction adds to a series of high-value apartment purchases in Juhu, an established luxury residential market that is also home to several Bollywood stars. Lodha Avalon, in particular, has attracted a string of wealthy buyers, including pharmaceutical companies and their senior executives.

"Pharma leaders buying marquee homes is an unmistakable trend across Mumbai's luxury landscape today. With solid business earnings and high conviction, corporate promoters are decisively locking in rare, large floor plates in premier seaside locations as generational assets," said Sandeep Reddy, co-founder of Zapkey.

In July, Mehul Shah, founder, chairman and managing director of pharmaceutical company Encube Ethicals, and his wife Niti Shah bought an apartment in Lodha Avalon for more than Rs.106 crore, at Rs.1.08 lakh per sq. ft.

In August, businessman Ravi Kishorilal Jhunjhunwala and his wife, Sarita R. Jhunjhunwala, purchased an apartment in the project for Rs.113.42 crore. Another transaction exceeding Rs.100 crore took place in 2025, when directors of financial consulting firm Sahastraa Advisors bought an apartment for Rs.106 crore.

A Lodha spokesperson declined to comment. Gufic spokespersons could not be immediately reached.

Mumbai's ultra-rich continue to favour luxury homes in established, sea-facing neighbourhoods such as Malabar Hill and Worli in South Mumbai, as well as Juhu and Bandra West in the suburbs. Limited availability of premium properties and their perceived long-term investment appeal continue to support demand in these markets.

data.title: Smriti Mandhana opens up on MS Dhoni's rare WhatsApp message after India's maiden 2025 Women's World Cup win | Watch
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- it has shared a quiet but meaningful moment from the night India finally won their maiden Women's ODI World Cup. Speaking alongside MS Dhoni at Gulf Oil Lubricants' 125th-anniversary event in Mumbai this week, the India captain revealed that Dhoni sent her a WhatsApp message after the November 2, 2025, final and asked her to pass his wishes to the entire team.

Mandhana, who took over the captaincy from Harmanpreet Kaur earlier this month, said the message stood out because Dhoni is known for keeping his phone use to a minimum.

"He actually did send me a message after the World Cup win. I know he doesn't use his phone a lot. I was very happy that he used WhatsApp to congratulate all of us," Smriti Mandhana said on stage.

The exchange came up during a conversation at the Mumbai event, where the two brand ambassadors shared the stage. Mandhana confirmed she already had Dhoni's number saved, a detail that drew a light reaction from the presenter.

MS Dhoni explained that Smriti Mandhana was the only player from the women's team whose number he had. The two had recently shot a commercial together, which is how the contact was available.

"I didn't know anyone else's (number) from the team. I wanted the message to go through. We had just shot (a commercial) before that. I thought, 'Let me send a message to Smriti', and I mentioned, 'Please wish everyone who is part of the team," Dhoni said.

He made it clear the congratulations were meant for the whole squad, not just one player. By routing the message through Mandhana, he ensured it reached the group that had just ended India's long wait for a senior women's World Cup title.

MS Dhoni also spoke about the wider impact of the win. India beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final at DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai, with Shafali Verma's 87 and Deepti Sharma's all-round effort (58 and 5/39) leading the way. Smriti Mandhana herself finished the tournament as India's leading run-scorer with 434 runs.

"It (the World Cup triumph) is a big thing. It changes how Indian women's cricket moves forward. Not only the fact that you have brought a big trophy for the country. It's the fact that these girls paved the way for future ladies and how they would look at cricket and treat it as a profession," Dhoni added.

The conversation at the Gulf Oil event offered a small window into how the 2025 triumph continues to resonate more than a year later, both inside the dressing room and beyond it.

data.title: Infosys Hyderabad Pocharam campus: New 1.1 million sq ft block adds 10,000 seats, supports 13,000 employees
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Infosys has inaugurated a new 1.1 million sq ft software development block at its Hyderabad Pocharam campus, adding 10,000 seats and enabling the IT major to accommodate an additional workforce of more than 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model.

The expansion is expected to strengthen the company's ability to scale its operations and support growing demand for technology services, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and engineering, according to PTI.

Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, IT and Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu and Infosys leadership attended the inauguration ceremony on Friday.

Spread across 450 acres, the Infosys Pocharam Development Centre has seven existing software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq ft of built-up area, according to a company release.

With the addition of the latest facility, the campus now has eight software development blocks, taking its total built-up area to approximately 5.68 million sq ft.

The new block's 10,000 seats are designed to support over 13,000 employees through a hybrid working arrangement, allowing Infosys to accommodate a larger workforce without requiring all employees to be present on campus simultaneously.

The development centre caters to global clients across Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), retail, life sciences and manufacturing.

The latest expansion will further enhance the company's capabilities in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services.

Despite the quarterly revenue growth, Infosys lowered its revenue growth forecast for the financial year, projecting constant-currency growth of 1% to 2%, against its earlier estimate of 1.5% to 3%.

Its operating margin remained stable at 21% year-on-year. Infosys retained its full-year operating margin guidance at 20% to 22%.

data.title: Binance says 90% of stolen crypto assets replenished after $6.3 billion security breach
data.description:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from a $6.3 billion security breach, with around 90% of the stolen token assets already replenished. The exchange said it is working to restore withdrawal services in phases.

In its second security incident recovery update, Binance said it would absorb the entire financial impact of the theft through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury, ensuring that users do not bear the losses.

"Our last update explained that Binance had set aside more than $6.34B in company funds to cover hacked losses, and we had already covered approximately 80% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss at that time," the exchange said in a statement.

"That covered amount is now up to 90%," it added.

Binance said Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), Tether (USDT), BNB, Solana (SOL), USD Coin (USDC), XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC were fully backed. It would continue buying the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter (OTC) channels until coverage reached 100% for all tokens.

The exchange said it had already secured $5 billion in the same digital assets that were stolen, including USDC, USDT, Bitcoin, Ether and BNB. In its earlier update, this represented approximately 80% of the impacted amount.

Binance confirmed that its hot wallets were compromised at around 20:05 UTC on October 29, resulting in unauthorised withdrawals of approximately $6.3 billion worth of digital assets.

As part of its recovery efforts, the exchange said around $3 billion in stolen assets had been frozen on blockchain networks through coordination with law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners.

The company said its technical team was targeting the phased resumption of withdrawals within approximately 34 hours, subject to the completion of security checks. Deposits and other unaffected platform services remained operational.

Binance also announced plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves report by Monday, November 2, allowing users to verify the digital assets backing their account balances.

On the cause of the breach, the exchange said its initial investigation had pointed to a compromised laptop, but subsequent findings had revealed additional points of intrusion.

"Our initial investigation suggested that the incident may involve a compromised laptop, however, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," it said.

The company reiterated that it had found no evidence of wallet private keys being leaked. Further technical findings were expected within approximately 48 hours, subject to verification.

Meanwhile, blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the $6.3 billion theft to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor, according to Reuters.

Cybersecurity experts cited by Reuters said proceeds from North Korean cryptocurrency thefts have helped fund the country's weapons programmes.

Binance has not publicly confirmed who was responsible for the attack and said its investigation remains ongoing.

The exchange said it would publish a detailed technical report outlining how the breach occurred and the additional security measures being introduced to prevent similar incidents.

data.title: He Lost His Job Over a Year Ago. Now He Asks for Help With His Financial Plan — WSJ
data.description:
By Lisa Ward

Kevin McCann is actively looking for a new job. In the meantime, he wants to make sure he is managing his savings wisely.

The 44-year-old from Chicago lost his position as a senior product manager at a tech startup over a year ago, where he earned upward of $200,000 a year including bonuses. He currently earns $20,000 from freelancing. His unemployment benefits ran out last November.

McCann, who is unmarried, has two 401(k)s from his previous employers totaling about $260,000 and a traditional IRA with about $160,000; the accounts are invested in about 80% equities and 20% fixed income. He is considering converting one or both of the accounts to a Roth IRA to take advantage of his current low income, which would mitigate the taxes he would owe on the conversion.

He already has a Roth with about $81,000, about $10,000 of which is in cash that could be used in an emergency. With the Roth, McCann can withdraw his original after-tax contribution without an early-withdrawal penalty or any additional taxes.

He also has almost $270,000 in a brokerage account. About $94,000 is invested in U.S. Treasury bonds that mature in one to six months, which he currently is tapping to supplement his income.

He has about $7,000 in a checking account, $6,000 in a health savings account and about $13,000 in six-month Series I savings bonds.

McCann owns a condo currently valued at about $625,000, with a $344,000 mortgage and a 2.99% interest rate. He pays $2,600 monthly, including taxes and HOA fees, and the mortgage is his only debt outstanding.

Other monthly expenses include $1,400 for groceries, eating out and entertainment, $150 for gas and public transportation, $200 for general shopping and $250 every six months for car insurance.

McCann currently has no health insurance. He looked at buying a high-deductible plan, but the plans cost about $400 a month, which he thought was too high given his current circumstances.

He says he has reduced his spending from $7,000 to $5,000 monthly since the job loss.

Advice from a pro

Jarrett Solomon, a certified financial planner and partner at Connecticut Wealth Management in Farmington, Conn., suggests McCann first rethink his decision to forgo health insurance. Paying $400 monthly for a high-deductible plan or looking for catastrophic coverage is worthwhile, he says, because an unexpected serious illness or injury could drastically alter McCann's financial well-being if he lacks coverage.

Solomon doesn't recommend converting either the 401(k) or traditional IRA into a Roth, because the taxes he would owe on the money he withdraws for the conversion might be too costly for McCann right now, even though he's currently in a lower tax bracket than he will be when he finds full-time employment.

Similarly, Solomon suggests McCann hold off on contributing to the HSA even if he decides to buy a high-deductible health plan. The money can only be used for qualifying healthcare expenses (otherwise income tax is owed on the amount withdrawn, and there's a steep penalty if you are under age 65), and he needs to be able to easily access his savings right now.

One move McCann can make to take advantage of temporarily being in a lower income-tax bracket is to sell some of his most profitable mutual funds in his taxable brokerage account and buy them back.

That could help reduce capital-gains taxes he might owe in the future, when his income is higher, because any gains at that point would be calculated from the price he pays for the funds now, rather than the lower price he paid earlier. And he wouldn't have to pay federal capital-gains taxes on the sale now as long as his taxable income is lower than $50,000, though he might still have to pay state tax.

He also might choose to keep some of the proceeds from the sale more liquid in case finding a new job takes longer than expected.

Solomon says McCann should look for ways to reduce monthly expenses, particularly on food and utilities.

Finally, Solomon suggests McCann can maximize long-term growth in his retirement accounts by investing more aggressively — changing the asset allocation to 90% or even 100% equities. He can use the brokerage account for more-conservative fixed-income investments as well as cash.

data.title: Muthoot Finance posts 27% rise in PAT at ₹2,977 crore  in Q2 FY27
data.description:
Gold loan lender Muthoot Finance Ltd has registered a 27 per cent increase in its profit after tax (PAT) at ₹2,977 crore as against ₹2,345 crores in Q2 FY26.

The company registered a PAT of ₹5,527 crore in H1 FY27 as against ₹4,391 crore in H1 FY26, an increase of 26 per cent y-o-y. Loan AUM stood at ₹1,87,810 crore in H1 FY27 as compared to ₹1,32,305 crore in H1 FY26, registering a growth of 42 per cent y-o-y. During Q2 FY27, gold loan AUM increased by ₹15,658 crore.

data.title: Rainbow Children’s Medicare Q2: Revenue rises 23%, profit grows 11%
data.description:
Rainbow Children’s Medicare reported a 23% year-on-year increase in revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The firm reported revenue of 548 crore, up from 444 crore same quarter last year.

EBITDA grew 14%, while profit after tax (PAT) rose 11% during the quarter. PAT came at 83.9 crore compare to 75.6 crore last year.

The company said inpatient and outpatient volumes remained healthy despite seasonal softness due to a significant shortfall in monsoon rainfall. It attributed the growth to patient volumes, improving performance across hospitals and initiatives focused on digital engagement and community outreach.

Rainbow said these initiatives are translating into higher outpatient department (OPD) footfalls and inpatient admissions.

Expansion in Andhra Pradesh

The company has commenced operations at a newly acquired 70-bed hospital in Nellore and a new 50-bed hospital in Guntur, strengthening its presence in Coastal Andhra Pradesh. These additions extend its network from Visakhapatnam to Chennai.

Rainbow also plans to establish a specialised paediatric hospital in Amaravati in phases, with an initial capacity of 150 beds. The project follows the allotment of two acres of land by the Andhra Pradesh government and is currently in the planning phase.

The company said its recently launched hospitals in Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh, and HRBR, Mahadevapura and Electronic City in Bengaluru are progressing as expected and have been integrated into its operating model.

Updates on upcoming projects

Rainbow expects to commence operations at its Indore hospital in Q3 FY27. At its Malad facility in Mumbai, project work has been completed and interior work is underway, with operations targeted for Q1 FY28.

Construction of its approximately 130-bed regional hub hospital in Coimbatore is progressing, with operations expected to begin in Q3 FY28. The company is also developing two facilities in Gurugram — a 125-bed spoke hospital in Sector 56, targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY28, and a 325-bed hub hospital in Sector 44, expected to begin operations in Q1 FY29.

Development work is continuing on a 150-bed regional hub hospital in Pune and an 80-bed spoke hospital in Seegehalli, both of which are expected to commence operations in FY29.

Commenting on the performance, Chairman and Managing Director Ramesh Kancharla said the expansion in Nellore and Guntur strengthens the company's presence across Andhra Pradesh, while the proposed Amaravati hospital has moved into the project planning phase.

CEO Abarali Dalal said the company had recorded year-on-year revenue growth of more than 20% for the third consecutive quarter. He attributed the performance to the onboarding of doctors, healthy occupancy and operational efficiencies, adding that new hospitals were steadily ramping up and contributing to network growth.

Rainbow said its focus remains on improving occupancy, maintaining patient throughput and sustaining growth across mature and new hospitals.

Rainbow Children’s Medicare shares ended 2.27% higher at ₹1,224 on October 30, gaining ₹27.20.

data.title: Marketing industry leaders and experts explore AI impact at VIT Chennai Marketing Conclave
data.description:
The VIT Business School, VIT Chennai on Friday organised a Marketing Conclave bringing together industry leaders, marketing professionals and entrepreneurs to explore consumer behaviour, brand building and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence (AI).

The event saw Lakshminarayanan Duraiswamy, Managing Director, Sundaram Home Finance Limited, deliver the keynote address, and LV Navneeth, Chief Executive Officer, THG Publishing Private Ltd (The Hindu), also delivered a special keynote address.

Emphasising the importance of customer trust in an increasingly AI-driven business environment, Duraiswamy said that organisations must earn customers’ trust and continue to strengthen it every day. Technology and innovation should always be guided by customer needs, he said.

“AI is not about creating a new technology, and it is not about creating a new design. It is about what it does for the customer,” he added.

Imagining the Future

Speaking on the theme “Imagining the Future", Navneeth urged young people to cultivate the ability to reflect, imagine and execute ideas. The constant pressure to remain busy often leaves little time for meaningful reflection, which is essential for innovation and creative thinking, he observed.

Thyagarajan T, Pro-Vice Chancellor, VIT Chennai; Suresh Balakrishna, Consultant, VIT Chennai; and Saju B, Dean, VIT Business School, VIT Chennai, also addressed the gathering.

The conclave featured three panel discussions and two fireside chats, providing a platform for industry experts to exchange perspectives on emerging marketing trends, changing consumer expectations and the impact of technology on brand strategy.

The first panel discussion, titled “The Human Edge: Understanding Consumers in the Age of AI", examined the continuing importance of human understanding and consumer insights in technology-driven marketing. The second panel explored strategies for building meaningful consumer relationships and lasting brand loyalty.

Another panel focused on the changing branding landscape, examining the challenges and opportunities emerging from the growth of direct-to-consumer (D2C) business models.

The Marketing Conclave also provided a forum for students and industry professionals to exchange ideas on the future of marketing.

data.title: Birla Corporation Q2 profit plunges 58.9% to ₹37 crore on higher input costs
data.description:
Birla Corporation Ltd on Saturday reported a 58.9 per cent year-on-year moderation in consolidated net profit to Rs 37 crore for the September quarter, as higher input costs and weak cement prices hit margins.

The company had posted a net profit of Rs 90 crore in the same period a year ago.

Revenue rises, but EBITDA declines

Consolidated revenue rose 9 per cent to Rs 2,441 crore from Rs 2,233 crore a year earlier. Consolidated EBITDA declined to Rs 254 crore from Rs 332 crore.

Cement sales volume grew 7 per cent to 4.54 million tonnes, while realisation rose 2 per cent to Rs 4,925 per tonne, though it was marginally lower sequentially as prices weakened in core markets through July and August. Capacity utilisation was steady at 85 per cent.

Higher input costs squeeze cement margins

Clinker cost rose 13 per cent, and power and fuel cost went up 15 per cent as pet coke prices climbed 64 per cent. The cement division’s EBITDA per tonne fell to Rs 482 from Rs 712, and its EBITDA margin contracted 490 basis points to 9.8 per cent.

Blended cement made up 86 per cent of sales, while premium products grew 17 per cent to 2.38 million tonnes. The share of the trade channel rose to 82 per cent from 79 per cent.

Green power and coal mine to help contain costs

To contain costs, the company raised green power consumption to 32 per cent from 30 per cent and began extracting coal from its Bikram mine in Madhya Pradesh. The mine is expected to deliver 1.8 lakh tonnes in the second half of the fiscal.

Jute division reports higher revenue and cash profit

In the jute division, revenue rose 17 per cent to Rs 155 crore, and cash profit stood at Rs 13.01 crore against Rs 4.64 crore a year ago, despite a 26 per cent drop in production due to raw jute shortage.

For the first half, net profit fell 27.1 per cent to Rs 153 crore, while revenue rose 8.3 per cent to Rs 5,111 crore.

The company said cement realisation has begun improving from October, but cost pressure is likely to persist and weigh on profitability.

data.title: LPG under recovery may rise to ₹370/cylinder in December 2026
data.description:
The under recovery on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is expected to rise by roughly 13 per cent on a monthly basis to ₹370 per 14.2 kg domestic cylinder in December 2026.

Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) Director (Finance) Anuj Jain in a post-results analyst call on Saturday said that under recovery on LPG is around ₹309 per domestic cylinder in November 2026 and is likely to hit ₹370 during December.

“The Saudi CP has gone up to $756 per tonne. So as far as my under recovery is concerned, in September 2026 it was ₹184 per cylinder, which went up to ₹229 in October and going forward in the month of November, we see that it would be somewhere in the range of ₹309 per cylinder. In December, it may go to ₹370 per cylinder,” he added.

As of September 30, 2026, IOCL’s cumulative under recovery on LPG was ₹32,505.69 crore.

The other two PSU oil marketing companies, Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) reported under recoveries of ₹17,334.40 crore and ₹18,048.82 crore, respectively.

Under recoveries rise on lower rates

The OMCs are saddled with huge under recoveries on account of selling the cooking fuel--used by more than 33 crore households--at below the prevailing market rates.

IOCL’s September quarter (FY27) net profit more than doubled to around ₹22,503 crore as lower crude oil prices and higher refining margins helped off-set losses from selling petrol, diesel and LPG below market rates.

The country’s largest fuel retailer said that Q2 FY27 profitability was largely driven by temporary decline in crude oil prices from mid-June to mid-August and robust margins from petrochemicals and gas.

“However, profitability in upcoming quarters may be adversely impacted by inventory losses due to potential fall in crude oil prices with normalization of the situation in the Middle East,” it has warned.

data.title: Jaipur Court rejects Inventiva publisher Nitin Naresh's anticipatory bail in Terra Invest case
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- In a significant development in the ongoing legal dispute involving Terra Invest founders Ankiti Bose and Krishan Rattan, a Jaipur sessions court has rejected the anticipatory bail plea of Inventiva publisher Nitin Naresh in a criminal case arising from allegations of extortion, criminal intimidation and conspiracy linked to communications concerning the investment firm.

Additional Sessions Judge Renuka Singh Hudda, Jaipur Metropolitan-II, passed the order on October 28, observing that the material on record and the circumstances of the case did not warrant pre-arrest protection while the investigation remained incomplete. The court also took note of separate Delhi High Court proceedings concerning disputed publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest.

The case stems from a complaint filed by a representative of Terra Vision Investments LLC, who alleged that threatening emails demanded money in exchange for refraining from publishing further adverse material concerning the investment firm and individuals associated with it.

The court considered allegations relating to emails dated August 26 and September 3, 2026, and a payment of Rs.11,700 allegedly deposited into a bank account held in the name of Nine Network Private Limited, the company that owns Inventiva.

The order refers to earlier Delhi High Court proceedings concerning publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest, including its founding partners Bose and Rattan. However, the bail ruling does not establish that the alleged conduct formed part of a wider conspiracy targeting the founders.

According to the complaint detailed in the order, the complainant is the India representative of Terra Vision Investments LLC and operates the investment firm's official email account.

The complainant alleged that emails received on August 26 and September 3, 2026, demanded money and threatened further adverse publications if the demands were not met.

According to the complaint, Rs.11,700 was deposited through a cash deposit machine at an HDFC Bank branch in Jaipur on September 3 into an account held in the name of Nine Network Private Limited. The complainant alleged that the payment was made in the hope that the demands and threats would stop, but another demand followed shortly afterwards.

The court observed that the case diary and material placed before it indicated a connection between the alleged demands, the threat of further publications and the amount deposited into the company's account.

It also noted Naresh's defence that the account was operated online and that the money had been deposited into it without his knowledge. However, the court observed that the record did not contain material showing that he had attempted to return the amount on that basis.

Naresh's counsel denied that he had sent the emails, demanded money or threatened the complainant. The defence also argued that there was no evidence establishing that the email account used to make the alleged demands belonged to him.

Counsel further submitted that Naresh was cooperating with the investigation, that his arrest was unnecessary and that he was willing to comply with any conditions imposed by the court.

The prosecution and the complainant's representatives opposed the plea, arguing that the allegations were serious and that further investigation remained necessary.

The Jaipur court referred to three civil suits before the Delhi High Court in which interim orders had been passed concerning publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest.

The order records that Naresh and other defendants had been restrained from publishing further material covered by the Delhi High Court's directions where such publications could interfere with the plaintiffs' legal rights.

The earlier proceedings included interim orders dated August 24 and September 14, 2026, concerning specified articles and further publications allegedly containing defamatory imputations against individuals associated with the investment firm.

The proceedings form part of the wider legal dispute involving Inventiva and Terra Invest, including individuals associated with the investment firm such as Ankiti Bose and Krishan Rattan.

However, the Delhi High Court's interim orders concern the civil claims before it and do not, by themselves, establish the criminal allegations being investigated in Jaipur. The Jaipur court considered the earlier proceedings while examining the circumstances of the dispute and the allegations forming the basis of the criminal complaint.

The order records that, according to the case diary, Naresh allegedly threatened the complainant's advocate outside court on October 26, 2026.

The court noted that advocate Garvit Khandelwal had lodged a separate complaint against Naresh at Sadar Police Station in Jaipur on the same date in connection with the alleged threat.

The allegation was among the circumstances referred to in the order while the court considered the anticipatory bail application. The separate complaint does not, by itself, establish that the alleged threat occurred.

After considering the material and the rival submissions, the court observed that the dispute between the parties concerned adverse publications and communications, while the present criminal case related to allegations of money being demanded in exchange for refraining from publishing such material.

The court referred to Supreme Court judgments on anticipatory bail, including the need to consider the nature and gravity of the allegations, the presumption of innocence and the requirements of an effective investigation.

It held that the circumstances of the case did not justify granting Naresh pre-arrest protection while further investigation remained pending.

The court accordingly dismissed his application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

The FIR, registered at Shastri Nagar Police Station in Jaipur, invokes Sections 308(2), 308(3), 351(2), 61(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

The rejection of anticipatory bail is not a conviction or a final determination of guilt. The allegations against Naresh and the other accused remain subject to investigation and adjudication in accordance with law.

data.title: Binance says its top 10 user assets are fully backed after security incident
data.description:
Binance says the 10 assets its users hold most are now backed 1:1. The list covers BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC.

That is normally a routine reassurance. This time it follows a security incident that reportedly cost the exchange around $6.34 billion, so the statement carries more weight than usual.

The confirmation came on October 31, 2026. Binance said the top 10 user assets are fully covered after it resolved the losses from the incident.

The research for this report says the exchange has covered approximately 90% of the total impact. The money came from a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), plus corporate funds.

The remaining 10% is still open. Those losses are mostly tied to lower-liquidity tokens, and Binance is still buying them back through market and OTC channels.

The list itself is worth a look. Four of the 10 assets are dollar-pegged stablecoins: USDT, USDC, USD1, and RLUSD. The rest mix the two largest crypto assets, Binance's own BNB, SOL, XRP, and ZEC.

Binance published a new Proof of Reserves (PoR) snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31, 2026. A more detailed verification proof is anticipated by November 3, 2026.

That proof is expected to use zk-SNARKs and Merkle trees. The goal is to let users confirm independently that their balances are backed 1:1 or better.

The previous snapshot gives a useful baseline. On October 1, 2026, reserve ratios for major assets sat at or above 100%.

BTC came in at 100.35%. ETH sat right on the line at 100.00%, and USDT was at 103.88%.

Customer assets on Binance totaled approximately $129.4 billion as of early October. On-chain reserves came to about $135.8 billion, slightly above net liabilities.

The October 31 snapshot should show how those ratios held up after the incident. The November 3 proof is when outside verification becomes possible.

Withdrawals were paused during an internal security review. They are scheduled to restart on November 1, 2026, in phases, one token at a time.

For users, the order of events matters. Binance announced the backing on October 31, withdrawals begin reopening November 1, and the verification proof is expected by November 3.

Customers will be able to move some funds before they can check the cryptographic proof.

The biggest open item is the 10% of losses not yet covered. Binance says the gap sits mostly in lower-liquidity tokens, so major holdings appear protected while holders of smaller assets wait.

The verification proof is the next real test. A full backing claim on October 31 is a statement, while a checkable proof on November 3 is evidence.

There are limits to keep in mind. Proof of reserves shows assets on hand at a moment in time, and its value depends on the liabilities side being complete and accurate.

For now, the claim is clear and the timeline is set. Users should watch three things: the order in which tokens reopen, the November 3 proof, and whether the remaining 10% gets closed out.

data.title: Healthcare Earnings Scoreboard: 96% beat EPS estimates, 70% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Healthcare companies reported broadly positive Q3 results last week, with every S&P 500 healthcare stock that posted results showing Y/Y topline growth, although earnings growth was less consistent.

Heathcare Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 23 companies reporting, 22 firms (96%) exceeded EPS expectations, while 1 fell short. Notably, 16 firms (70%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 23 companies reporting, 21 firms (91%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, all 23 firms (100%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.

Let’s take a look at some of the healthcare companies that reported earnings this week:

AbbVie reported Q3 revenue of $17.40B, up 10.3% Y/Y, beating the $17.35B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $3.82 beat the $3.77 estimate. Growth was driven by strong sales of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which rose 22.7% and 23.9%, respectively. The company raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95–$13.99 from $13.76–$13.96.

Eli Lilly reported Q3 revenue of $24.40B, up 39% Y/Y, beating the $22.42B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $7.48 beat the $5.60 estimate. Growth was driven by strong demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $91B–$92B.

Bristol Myers Squibb  reported Q3 revenue of $13.07B, up 7% Y/Y, beating consensus, while adjusted EPS of $1.35 topped the $1.09 estimate. Growth was driven by its Growth Portfolio, particularly Eliquis, which generated $4.69B in sales, up 25% Y/Y. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook but lowered its adjusted EPS forecast to $6.35–$6.55.

Gilead Sciences reported Q3 revenue of $8.30B, up 7% Y/Y, beating the $7.79B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.55 beat the $2.17 estimate. HIV medicines drove growth, with Biktarvy sales rising 10% to $4.1B. Trodelvy sales increased 42% to $506M. Gilead raised its FY2026 product sales outlook to $31B–$31.3B.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported Q3 revenue of $5.12B, up 36% Y/Y, beating the $4.56B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $20.07 beat the $16.25 estimate. Growth was driven by strong sales of Dupixent (up 35%), Eylea HD (up 62%) and Libtayo (up 51%).

Biogen reported Q3 revenue of $2.8B, up 11% Y/Y, beating the $2.63B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.62 topped the $1.98 estimate. Growth Portfolio revenue surged 49% to $1.26B, while Spinraza sales rose 23% to $461M. The company raised the lower end of its FY2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $12.20.

Illumina reported Q3 revenue of $1.13B, up 4.2% Y/Y. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.43 versus $0.98 a year earlier. Clinical demand and NovaSeq X placements supported growth. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $4.64B–$4.66B and non-GAAP EPS outlook to $5.40–$5.45.

Earnings next week

For the upcoming week, investors will continue to watch healthcare earnings, including reports from Amgen , Pfizer , Vertex Pharmaceuticals , Novo Nordisk and others.

data.title: Vietnam to cut retail electricity price by 2% from November 1

Vietnam will cut its average retail electricity price by 2% from November 1 to support economic stability and reduce costs for households and businesses, the government said on Saturday.
